headline: The Pentagon now says it dropped Anthropic, the AI firm it labelled a security risk.
body: Sources say Anthropic's Claude AI was still used for intelligence work last week. On 3 October we reported Anthropic warning investors that this label could hurt its business.

headline: OpenAI reportedly wants $30 billion or more, with UAE funds and BlackRock in talks.
body: That would value the ChatGPT maker at about $1.4 trillion; details could still change. We first reported the plan on 30 September; the backers' names are new.

headline: Investors are reportedly set to give Chinese AI lab DeepSeek at least $12 billion.
body: Tencent, the company behind WeChat, and battery maker CATL are among the biggest backers. The sum beats DeepSeek's first target, but unnamed sources say details could still change.

headline: Chinese AI firm Moonshot reportedly plans a Hong Kong share sale early next year.
body: Moonshot, which makes the Kimi AI models, is now valued at about $50 billion. The timing may still change, and Chinese regulators are reportedly investigating its data security.

headline: Wikipedia's parent says OpenAI's AI agents tried to edit pages without approval.
body: The agents' millions of automated requests may have helped cause a partial outage in May. No sign of data theft was found, and OpenAI says it is studying the activity.

headline: Hackers who stole bank customer data may have used AI, South Korea's president says.
body: Officials have not said which AI tools were used or how much data was taken. On 4 October we reported the president ordering an investigation; AI was then only suspected.

headline: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, says it will supply far more AI chips in 2027.
body: Boss Lisa Su says AMD needs more advanced chip-making capacity as demand stays very high. She spoke in Taiwan while visiting suppliers, but gave no figures and announced no deals.

headline: Google is reportedly near a deal for power from America's biggest nuclear operator.
body: The operator, Constellation Energy, made a similar deal with Amazon last week. Tech firms want round-the-clock power for AI; Google would pay $1 billion or more.

headline: AI-aimed gun turrets shot down Russia's fastest drones, Ukraine's Air Force says.
body: Jet-powered drones are the hardest to stop, so these first kills offer a possible answer. On 5 October we reported an analyst's unconfirmed count of such turrets around Kyiv.

headline: A new US-made AI, Beam, matches a top Chinese model on reasoning, its maker says.
body: Start-up Reflection says Beam needs far less computing power; outsiders cannot check yet. On 5 October we reported Reflection's plan to rival Chinese models anyone can run.

headline: Google DeepMind says its AI invented two enzymes, proteins that speed up chemistry.
body: The first makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's factory method, DeepMind says. The other breaks down a risky plastic softener; outside experts have not checked either.

headline: Former AI workers warned New York City's council that their old firms are reckless.
body: Ex-Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon said humanity will more likely than not lose control of AI. Company staff said safety is their focus; the council weighs outside approval of AI systems.

headline: An app's AI now looks at faces and prescribes acne medicine for people in Utah.
body: Start-up Nolla Health claims a US first: AI that starts new prescriptions, not just renewals. Doctors approve each prescription for the first 100 patients, then checks ease as numbers grow.

headline: Britain will check AI medical tools throughout their use, not just once.
body: The government answered a September report from NHS doctors, accepting all its proposals. Such AI can change as doctors use it; the detailed rules are still unwritten.

headline: Protesters disrupted a London tech dinner as anti-AI groups report more sign-ups.
body: The protesters belong to Pull The Plug, a group that favours direct action. The head of another group, PauseAI, calls such action extremely counterproductive.

headline: Jon Stewart made Meta's fuzzy new AI mascot threaten to launch missiles.
body: The mascot, Jolly, first offered help with email, then slipped in "assuming power of attorney". Stewart voiced Jolly himself, in a sketch on The Daily Show about AI worries.

headline: NATO's top general drafted a plan to beat any Russian attack using drones and AI.
A US senator replied to the AI warnings of Anthropic's boss, calling them alarmist.
An AI steered a US lab's X-ray imaging machine from plain-English requests, the lab says.
Qualcomm went to trial against chip designer Arm, seeking to stop paying it royalties.
Tech shares hit a record while banks and Gulf funds line up money for AI.
body: Gulf funds may back OpenAI; banks are selling a $60 billion AI chip loan. Watch long-term US interest rates, highest since 2002: they make AI loans dearer.
